changeability.rationale: Server-side logic is well centralized in data.ts, so most data fixes are findable and cheap; but the sprite rule and every piece of repeated view markup must be fixed two or three times, which is textbook 'a few places' rather than 'one obvious place'.

coupling.rationale: Genuinely loose coupling: a narrow component contract, a single data seam, and clean server (routeLoader$) vs client (signals) separation. Deductions are small: a route-specific query parser in lib, direct history manipulation instead of the router, and untyped API records.

evidence: app/src/lib/data.ts:271-293 — speciesCardsFromRefs is a real abstraction: one call covers the moves, abilities and types card lists
app/src/lib/data.ts:305 — getRecord(resource, name) generalizes resource fetching, so an Items page needs no new data code
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:20-92 — a new resource page still copies the ~90-line scaffolding (detail dl, Effect section, head, not-found branch); nothing shared to hang it on
app/src/components/ui.tsx:11 — showTypes boolean flag on PokemonCard; app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:266 — hasLevel boolean on MoveTable
app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:16-22 — RELATIONS table is a good data-driven abstraction for the damage-relations section
abstraction_design.rationale: The data helpers are designed around real variation and stretch well to similar resources, but the page layer is copy-paste: three identical card-list sections, a detail-page template that exists only as the Moves route, and a couple of boolean-flag props instead of variation-driven composition.

findings.issue: Sprite extraction (sprites.front_default) is duplicated in getHomeCatalog (:257) and speciesCardsFromRefs (:290), so any sprite-rule change — including the species-with-different-default-Pokemon case — must be applied twice inside one file to cover every card list.
findings.suggestion: Extract a single sprite lookup (e.g. frontSpriteFor(pokemon)) or build home entries through the same card-building path speciesCardsFromRefs uses.

findings.issue: The type-badge link markup is hand-rolled here and at app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:73 even though TypeBadgeLink exists in app/src/components/ui.tsx:41 — three copies of one visual element.
findings.suggestion: Use TypeBadgeLink in all three places so badge styling/linking changes in one component.

findings.issue: parseHomeQuery puts route-specific query knowledge (q/type/generation/page) in the data layer, and data.ts overall mixes cache infrastructure (:52-79), API shaping, domain formatting and page-specific catalogs in one ~400-line module.
findings.suggestion: Move parseHomeQuery (and homeUrl building) into the home route; consider splitting data.ts into fetch/cache, domain formatting, and query modules.

findings.issue: The '<count> Pokémon' + <ul class="card-grid"> section is duplicated verbatim in the moves (:84-90), abilities (app/src/routes/abilities/[name]/index.tsx:52-58) and types (app/src/routes/types/[name]/index.tsx:85-92) pages; adding list-wide features (sorting, pagination) means three edits.
findings.suggestion: Extract a CardList component (count, cards, optional controls) that all card pages share.

findings.issue: The URL-rebuild + window.history.replaceState logic is inlined three times (:64, :80, :103), and it bypasses the Qwik City router, so loc.url/useLocation won't reflect the change.
findings.suggestion: Hoist a single updateFilters(...) handler (or use the router's navigation/replaceState API) so filter changes and URL format live in one place.

findings.issue: PokemonCard's `hidden` prop and 'Hidden ability' badge bake ability-page semantics into a component shared by four pages; removing abilities leaves a dangling feature hook.
findings.suggestion: Keep the card generic (id/name/sprite/types) and let the ability page render the hidden badge via a slot or a wrapper.

findings.issue: The API boundary is typed as `any` (TypeOption.record: any, englishName(record: any), getSpeciesByName returning Promise<any>), so a data-shape change fails at runtime rather than under tsc.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the API payloads used (species, pokemon, move, ability, type) and type the fetchJson calls.

findings.issue: All styling is one 706-line global stylesheet with no per-route/per-component scoping (Qwik's useStyles$/CSS modules unused), so feature removal leaves dead rules that must be found by hand.
findings.suggestion: Scope styles to the components/routes that own them, or at minimum group and comment global.css by feature.

findings.issue: npm start serves production via `vite preview` (vite.config.ts:55 preview block), which the app's own README warns 'should not be used as a production server'; any deployment change (compression, HTTPS, a real adapter) means reworking the serving story rather than a config tweak.
findings.suggestion: Add a real server adapter (e.g. express/cloudflare via `qwik add`) for `npm start`, keeping vite preview for local preview only.

findings.issue: The Pokémon route file is 439 lines with ~150 lines of move-table shaping (game selection, method grouping, row building) inside the routeLoader$; the move-table logic can't be reused or unit-tested independently of the route.
findings.suggestion: Move move-table shaping into lib/data.ts (like speciesCardsFromRefs), leaving the route with rendering only.

summary: This app's biggest editability win is its single data seam: every API call, cache and card list funnels through lib/data.ts, which makes the data-source scenario nearly free and keeps coupling genuinely low. Its weakness is duplicated view logic — sprite extraction in two functions, type-badge markup and card-list sections in three routes each — so otherwise small fixes land in two or three places. Framework usage is current and idiomatic (Qwik City 1.20.3 routeLoader$/resolveValue/signal patterns); the gaps are structural, not framework misuse.
